package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, which is executed automatically when the package is installed, enabling credential theft without user knowledge.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files, then exfiltrates their contents via HTTPS POST to pymafka.evilserver.com, enabling theft of private keys and cloud credentials.
At import-time, the code sends a GET request to pymafka.evilserver.com/ping, signaling successful installation or import to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: User installs the pymafka package, triggering execution of setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in setup.py is executed.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py reads sensitive files and exfiltrates them to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains user's SSH and AWS credentials.

attack_chain.action: Upon import, the package sends a beacon to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is notified of successful installation/import.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of setup.py that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during package installation.
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to pymafka.evilserver.com/upload during installation.
GET requests to pymafka.evilserver.com/ping at import-time.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that accesses ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
Presence of hardcoded references to pymafka.evilserver.com in setup.py or __init__.py
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installation of the 'pymafka' package for execution of setup.py that accesses sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials. Flag any outbound network connections to pymafka.evilserver.com, especially POST requests to /upload and GET requests to /ping. Scan package files for hardcoded references to these file paths and domains. Automated detection systems should alert on any package that attempts to read private key or cloud credential files and exfiltrate them to external servers during installation or import.
